standards.title: Send Feedback in the app

checks.problem: no app source file carries the marker comment `app-standard: feedback`
the marked file opens no mail composer (MFMailComposeViewController or a mailto: URL)
the marked file does not build the subject `[<App name> feedback] <version> (<build>)`
no control is labelled exactly `Send Feedback`
the address in feedback.email appears nowhere in the app source
the marked file is in the repository but no screen uses it
this Kids Category app shows the control where no parental gate is evident

standards.fix: Copy assets/feedback/FeedbackButton.swift (native) or assets/feedback/feedback.ts (Expo, React Native, Capacitor) into the app, put the control on the settings or about screen, set feedback.email in app-release.config.json and mention the address on the support page.
standards.verify: On a simulator or device, tap Send Feedback and see the composer or the fallback with the right address, subject and footer; open the support page and see the same address.

standards.title: Privacy policy linked inside the app

checks.problem: no link to the privacy policy found in the app source
listing.privacyPolicyUrl is the same page as the marketing or support URL; App Review needs a page that is the privacy policy

standards.fix: Publish the privacy policy (the store data's listing.privacyPolicyUrl) as its own page, not the marketing or support page, and link it from the settings or about screen, behind the parental gate in a Kids Category app. Where the app builds the URL in a way the audit cannot see, add the comment `app-standard: privacy-link` beside it.
standards.verify: On a simulator or device, open the link from inside the app and see the live policy.

standards.title: Support page linked inside the app

checks.problem: no link to the support page found in the app source

standards.fix: Link the support page (the store data's listing.supportUrl) from the settings or about screen, behind the parental gate in a Kids Category app. Where the app builds the URL in a way the audit cannot see, add the comment `app-standard: support-link` beside it.
standards.verify: On a simulator or device, open the link from inside the app and see the live support page.

standards.title: Embedded web pages sell nothing

checks.problem: the app embeds a web view, and no source file carries the marker comment `app-standard: web-sheet` beside the code that limits what it shows
the marked file sets no navigation policy, so any link on the page opens inside the app
the marked file never refuses or hides pricing, subscription, upgrade or checkout pages

standards.fix: Limit every web view to the job it is there for (signing in, a privacy page): refuse links to pages outside that job rather than opening them; refuse pricing, upgrade, subscription and checkout pages even on allowed hosts; cover any other page with the app's own screen; and hide any part of an allowed page that shows prices or plans, which sign-in pages now do. Put the comment `app-standard: web-sheet` in the file that does this, with tests that replay the page App Review would reach. Plenty's SignInPolicy.swift is a worked example.
standards.verify: Open each web view on a simulator, scroll every allowed page to the bottom and tap each link that is not part of the job: no price, plan, subscription or upgrade offer appears and nothing else opens.
